headline: 1,935 hospitalised as five more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The national dengue death toll has risen to 294 this year, with 1,935 new admissions in a single day according to the DGHS.
details: At least five dengue patients died and 1,935 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the latest deaths, three were reported in the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) area and two in the Khulna division.
The total number of dengue deaths this year has now reached 294, while the total number of cases has climbed to 94,151.
Medicine specialist Dr ABM Abdullah noted that repeated infections, delayed diagnosis, and changes in clinical presentation are contributing to severe cases and deaths.
Dr Abdullah explained that dengue has four serotypes, meaning people infected for the first time may not recognize the symptoms, often mistaking them as influenza or other common illnesses.

headline_marked: Dhaka to launch [[two franchise bus routes in 7 days]] as part of city-wide overhaul
headline: Dhaka to launch two franchise bus routes in 7 days as part of city-wide overhaul
summary: The government plans to reorganize 418 approved routes into 32 franchise-based ones to improve discipline, vehicle fitness, and ticketing.
details: The government will introduce franchise-based bus services on two routes in Dhaka within seven working days, aiming for full operational status within six months.
Under this new system, a single designated company will operate each route, taking full responsibility for vehicle fitness, legal compliance, and driver discipline.
The plan involves reorganizing Dhaka's 418 approved bus routes into 32 streamlined routes, based on extensive surveys of over 45,000 passengers and drone filming of the network.
New features will include counter-based services, e-ticketing, and GPS tracking to modernize the city's public transport experience.
Bus owners have been ordered to repair and repaint all vehicles within two months; dilapidated buses that miss the deadline may be removed from the road.
Additionally, the BRTC is purchasing electric buses for eight proposed initial routes, and the government is exploring the feasibility of circular bus routes.
The meeting also addressed the disposal of approximately 36,000 seized vehicles to free up inadequate storage space and prevent further loss of value.
caption:
Dhaka's chaotic bus system is getting a major makeover. Two franchise routes launch in 7 days, with 32 to follow soon!

The government will introduce franchise-based bus services on two routes in Dhaka within seven working days, aiming for full operational status within six months.

Under this new system, a single designated company will operate each route, taking full responsibility for vehicle fitness, legal compliance, and driver discipline.

The plan involves reorganizing Dhaka's 418 approved bus routes into 32 streamlined routes, based on extensive surveys of over 45,000 passengers and drone filming of the network.

New features will include counter-based services, e-ticketing, and GPS tracking to modernize the city's public transport experience.

Bus owners have been ordered to repair and repaint all vehicles within two months; dilapidated buses that miss the deadline may be removed from the road.

Additionally, the BRTC is purchasing electric buses for eight proposed initial routes, and the government is exploring the feasibility of circular bus routes.

The meeting also addressed the disposal of approximately 36,000 seized vehicles to free up inadequate storage space and prevent further loss of value.
